answer: In PoA, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph: a verifier’s influence is the walk mass reaching identities. A sybil cluster hidden behind a sparse external cut has low conductance, so few walks cross its boundary; Cheeger-style bounds and min-cut transitivity therefore cap its aggregate voting weight, even when internally dense. This remains true across ferrous, terrace, or canyon-shaped graph regions.
